title: 20. Les robots vont changer l'économie
gist: The Economist argues that human-shaped robots are improving fast, getting much cheaper, and will probably start in homes doing chores before moving into factories, hospitals and building sites. That could hit manual jobs too, move factories, make many goods cheap and land and rent dearer. People may still be needed to run robots, but an unequal economy is also possible.

body.fr: Les robots {{humanoïdes|humanoid — human-shaped}} ont un corps {{comme|like}} un humain.

bd.meaning: Humanoid robots have a body like a human's.
chunks: humanoid robots — the adjective comes after the noun
a body (corps is spelled the same in the plural)
bd.key: Adjective after the noun: robots humanoïdes = “humanoid robots,” in the opposite order to English.

body.fr: L'IA {{a peut-être aidé|maybe helped}} à {{résoudre|solve}} un très vieux problème de maths.

bd.meaning: AI may have helped solve a very old maths problem.
chunks: maybe helped (a … aidé = past; peut-être sits in the middle)
un très vieux problème de maths
a very old maths problem — 'vieux' goes before the noun
bd.key: Past = avoir + past form: a aidé = “helped,” and little words like peut-être slip in between the two parts.

body.fr: Mais les robots {{ne savent pas bien|don't know how to … well}} {{plier un drap|fold a bedsheet}}.

bd.meaning: But robots still can't fold a bedsheet well.
chunks: don't know how to … well (savoir = know how to)
fold a sheet (plain verb after savoir)
bd.key: Negation sandwich + plain verb: ne … pas wraps savent, and the action plier stays plain after it.

body.fr: {{Bientôt|soon}}, ça va changer.

bd.meaning: Soon, that's going to change.
chunks: is going to change (aller + plain verb)
bd.key: Future = aller + plain verb: va changer = “is going to change.” Only va changes with the subject.

body.fr: Les robots {{progressent|are improving, making progress}} vite.

bd.meaning: Robots are getting better fast.
chunks: are making progress — the -ent ending marks a plural subject (it's silent)
bd.key: One present for two English ones: progressent covers both “improve” and “are improving.”

body.fr: Les {{ingénieurs|engineers}} utilisent les {{méthodes|methods}} de l'IA pour les robots.

bd.meaning: Engineers are using AI's methods for robots.
chunks: AI's methods (literally 'the methods of the AI')
bd.key: “de” = 's: French has no apostrophe-s, so les méthodes de l'IA = “AI's methods.”

body.fr: Et les prix {{baissent|are falling, going down}}.

bd.meaning: And prices are falling.
chunks: prices (prix is spelled the same in the plural)
bd.key: The little word “les” again: les prix = just “prices” — French keeps “the” where English drops it.

body.fr: En deux ans, le {{prix moyen|average price}} des robots d'une {{entreprise|company}} chinoise {{a baissé de|has fallen by}} 72 %.

bd.meaning: In two years, the average price of one Chinese company's robots has fallen by 72%.
chunks: the average price — 'moyen' after the noun
of a Chinese company's robots (des = de + les)
bd.key: Past = avoir + past form: a baissé = “has fallen / fell.” a is the helper, baissé the past form.

body.fr: La {{révolution|revolution}} des robots va {{probablement|probably}} commencer à la maison.

bd.meaning: The robot revolution will probably start at home.
chunks: the robot revolution (literally 'the revolution of the robots')
is probably going to start — 'probablement' sits between va and the plain verb
bd.key: aller + plain verb, with a word in the middle: va probablement commencer — the little extra word goes after va.

body.fr: {{Selon|according to}} des experts, {{il y aura|there will be}} peut-être un million de robots humanoïdes dans les maisons américaines {{d'ici|within, by}} 5 à 15 ans.

bd.meaning: According to experts, there may be a million humanoid robots in American homes within 5 to 15 years.
chunks: there will maybe be — il y aura = future of il y a
in American homes — adjective after the noun, agreeing (-es)
bd.key: il y a → il y aura: “there is” becomes “there will be.” Same set phrase, just pushed into the future.

body.fr: Ils vont faire les {{tâches ménagères|household chores}}, comme la {{lessive|laundry}} et la {{vaisselle|dishes}}.

bd.meaning: They'll do household chores, like the laundry and the dishes.
bd.key: faire = do / make: chores use faire — faire la vaisselle = “do the dishes.”

body.fr: {{Peu de gens|few people}} vont {{protester|object, protest}}.

bd.meaning: Few people will object.
chunks: are going to protest (aller + plain verb)
bd.key: peu de / beaucoup de: peu de gens = “few people,” the opposite of beaucoup de gens.

body.fr: C'est une bonne nouvelle, {{surtout|especially}} pour les femmes.

bd.meaning: It's good news, especially for women.
chunks: good news — 'bonne' goes before the noun
bd.key: “bon” goes BEFORE the noun and agrees: nouvelle is feminine, so bon becomes bonne.

body.fr: Ensuite, les robots vont arriver dans les {{usines|factories}}, dans les hôpitaux et sur les {{chantiers|building sites}}.

bd.meaning: Next, robots will arrive in factories, in hospitals and on building sites.
chunks: dans les usines, dans les hôpitaux
on building sites — French also says 'on' (sur) here
bd.key: Future = aller + plain verb: vont arriver = “are going to arrive.”

body.fr: Aujourd'hui, beaucoup de gens pensent que l'IA change {{seulement|only}} le travail de {{bureau|office}}.

bd.meaning: Today, many people think AI only changes office work.
chunks: that — French never drops it, unlike English
bd.key: “que” can't be dropped: English says “think AI…,” but French must say pensent que l'IA….

body.fr: Avec les robots, ce n'est plus vrai.

bd.meaning: With robots, that's no longer true.
chunks: it's no longer (c'est inside the ne … plus sandwich)
bd.key: ne … plus = “no longer”: same sandwich shape as ne … pas, but it means “not any more.”

body.fr: Un employé de bureau veut devenir {{électricien|electrician}} ou {{plombier|plumber}} ? Ce n'est peut-être pas une {{solution|solution, way out}}.

bd.meaning: An office worker wants to become an electrician or a plumber? That may not be a way out.
chunks: an electrician or a plumber — no 'un' before a job after devenir
Ce n'est peut-être pas une solution
bd.key: No article before a job: devenir électricien = “become an electrician” — French drops the un.

body.fr: Certains gouvernements vont peut-être {{réserver|keep, set aside}} des {{emplois|jobs}} aux humains.

bd.meaning: Some governments may keep certain jobs for humans.
bd.key: aux = à + les: à les never appears; it always fuses into aux.

body.fr: Bill Gates {{a proposé|proposed}} cette idée.

bd.meaning: Bill Gates has suggested this idea.
bd.key: Past = avoir + past form: a proposé — the -é ending marks the past form of an -er verb.

body.fr: Aujourd'hui, les voitures {{sans chauffeur|driverless}} arrivent {{lentement|slowly}}, parce que des chauffeurs de taxi et des {{responsables locaux|local officials}} sont {{contre|against (it)}}.

bd.meaning: Today, driverless cars are spreading slowly, because some taxi drivers and local officials are against them.
chunks: des chauffeurs de taxi et des responsables locaux
bd.key: sans + noun, no article: sans chauffeur = “without a driver,” just as sans avocat in story 1.

body.fr: Les robots vont peut-être avoir le même problème.

bd.meaning: Robots may face the same problem.
chunks: the same problem — 'même' before the noun = same
bd.key: le même = “the same”: before a noun, même means “same” (in story 1, alone at the start, it meant “even”).

body.fr: Mais ça ne va probablement pas les {{arrêter|stop}}.

bd.meaning: But it probably won't stop them.
chunks: is probably not going to (ne … pas around va)
stop them — 'les' (them) sits before the verb
bd.key: “them” goes before the verb: les arrêter = “stop them.” Here les is a pronoun, not “the.”

body.fr: Aujourd'hui, les usines vont dans les pays où le travail {{coûte|costs}} moins cher.

bd.meaning: Today, factories move to countries where labour is cheaper.
chunks: work costs less (coûter cher = be expensive)
bd.key: “où” = “where” and hooks a description onto a place: les pays où… = “the countries where…”

body.fr: Avec les robots, les {{salaires|wages}} vont moins {{compter|matter, count}}.

bd.meaning: With robots, wages will matter less.
bd.key: compter = “to matter” as well as “to count.” Ça compte = “it matters.”

body.fr: Le prix de la {{terre|land}} et de l'{{énergie|energy}} va compter plus.

bd.meaning: The price of land and energy will matter more.
chunks: de la terre et de l'énergie
of land and of energy — 'de' repeats before each noun
bd.key: Repeat the little word: French says de la terre et de l'énergie, repeating de where English says it once.

body.fr: Pour certains {{métiers|jobs, trades}}, rien n'a changé depuis des {{siècles|centuries}}.

bd.meaning: For some jobs, nothing has changed for centuries.
chunks: nothing has changed (rien … ne sandwich + avoir + past form)
bd.key: rien ne = “nothing”: when “nothing” is the subject, rien comes first and ne still goes before the verb.

body.fr: Par exemple, un {{quatuor|quartet}} {{a toujours besoin de|still needs}} quatre musiciens, comme à l'{{époque|time, era}} de Mozart.

bd.meaning: For example, a string quartet still needs four musicians, just as in Mozart's time.
chunks: still needs (avoir besoin de = need; toujours = still)
bd.key: avoir besoin de = “to need”: literally “to have need of.” Only avoir changes: il a besoin de.

body.fr: {{S'occuper des|taking care of}} personnes âgées, c'est pareil.

bd.meaning: Caring for older people is the same.
chunks: taking care of elderly people (des = de + les)
it's the same — very common in speech
bd.key: Plain verb as a subject, then c'est: S'occuper de…, c'est… = “Taking care of… is…”

body.fr: Les robots peuvent changer ça.

bd.meaning: Robots could change that.
bd.key: Helper + plain verb: peuvent changer — only peuvent conjugates.

body.fr: Beaucoup de choses vont devenir {{bon marché|cheap}}, comme les T-shirts.

bd.meaning: Lots of things will become cheap, like T-shirts.
chunks: cheap — a fixed phrase that never changes form
bd.key: bon marché never agrees: it stays the same with plural or feminine nouns — des choses bon marché.

body.fr: Mais la terre et les {{ressources naturelles|natural resources}} vont rester {{rares|scarce}} et chères.

bd.meaning: But land and natural resources will stay scarce and expensive.
chunks: la terre et les ressources naturelles
bd.key: Adjectives agree with the noun: ressources is feminine plural, so cher becomes chères.

body.fr: Les {{loyers|rents}} vont peut-être devenir {{encore plus|even more}} chers.

bd.meaning: Rents may get even more expensive.
chunks: even more expensive (encore plus = even more)
bd.key: plus + adjective = “more ___”: plus chers = “more expensive,” and encore adds “even.”

body.fr: {{Peut-être que|maybe}} les humains vont encore travailler : ils vont {{gérer|manage}} et {{réparer|repair}} les robots.

bd.meaning: Maybe humans will still work: they'll manage and repair the robots.
chunks: maybe — at the start of a sentence, add 'que'
humans are still going to work (encore = still)
they're going to manage and repair — one 'vont' covers both verbs
bd.key: One aller, two plain verbs: vont gérer et réparer — the helper isn't repeated.

body.fr: Et qui veut payer pour écouter un {{orchestre|orchestra}} de robots ?

bd.meaning: And who wants to pay to listen to a robot orchestra?
chunks: to listen to — écouter already includes 'to'
a robot orchestra (literally 'an orchestra of robots')
bd.key: écouter = “listen to”: no extra word needed — écouter un orchestre, not “écouter à.”

body.fr: L'autre possibilité : les robots travaillent pour les gens qui les {{possèdent|own}}.

bd.meaning: The other possibility: robots work for the people who own them.
chunks: who own them — 'les' (them) before the verb
bd.key: Two different “les”: les gens = “the people,” but in les possèdent it means “them,” sitting before the verb.

body.fr: Les autres sont en {{concurrence|competition}} avec les robots pour la terre et l'énergie.

bd.meaning: Everyone else competes with the robots for land and energy.
bd.key: être en + noun: être en concurrence = “to be competing,” a handy set shape.

body.fr: L'IA a {{surpris|surprised}} le monde.

bd.meaning: AI took the world by surprise.
bd.key: Past = avoir + past form: surprendre has an irregular past form, surpris.

body.fr: Les robots vont peut-être nous surprendre aussi.

bd.meaning: Robots may surprise us too.
bd.key: “us” before the verb: nous surprendre = “surprise us,” the same position as les earlier.

body.fr: {{Il faut|we need to, it's necessary to}} {{se préparer|get ready}}.

bd.meaning: We need to get ready.
chunks: it's necessary / we need to — a fixed phrase
bd.key: il faut + plain verb = “we / you need to.” A fixed phrase: the il doesn't mean “he.”

grammar.en: aller + plain verb = the near future. It runs through this whole story: va commencer, vont arriver, vont rester. Small words like peut-être or probablement slot in after aller.
avoir + past participle = the past (passé composé). a baissé, a proposé, a surpris. Your “past = avoir/être + verb” key.

grammar.fr: Ça ne va pas les arrêter
grammar.en: Object pronouns go before the verb. les (them) and nous (us) sit in front of the plain verb: les arrêter, nous surprendre. Don't confuse this les with “the.”

quiz.q: Où la révolution des robots va-t-elle probablement commencer ?
quiz.a: À la maison — les robots vont faire la lessive et la vaisselle. (At home — robots will do the laundry and the dishes.)

flag: Heavily compressed: this is an Economist opinion piece (“leader”), retold neutrally. I dropped the C-3PO and Marvin references, the Riemann hypothesis by name, the “doubling every two months” metric, migration and NIMBY points, Baumol by name, capital in the last point and most hedging nuance. Some “could” claims became va peut-être to stay at A1 (a native would often use the conditional pourrait). Ce n'est peut-être pas une solution loosely renders “might be out of luck”; responsables locaux is my choice for “local officials.”
